messages:
olivia: Running through the onboarding sample I bumped into a reproducible stream failure when we rotate tokens mid-generation. Long prompt, generator.Stream, then auth refresh. The iterator just stops with a generic EOF-like error.
kevin: Oof. Are you recreating the http.Client on refresh? That will tear TLS connections and the server can close the stream.
olivia: Yep — our KMS hook hands back a fresh creds object so sample recreated client to attach it. We did this to keep code simple for demos.
sam: Quick note for the sample app: that's the easy footgun. Better pattern is to keep one *transport* and inject the token at request time via a RoundTripper wrapping a token-provider func. That avoids connection churn.
olivia: Can you sketch the RoundTripper? I can swap sample code.
sam: Example (pseudo):
```go
type tokenFn func() string
rt := &AuthRT{Base: http.DefaultTransport, Token: tokenFn}
client := &http.Client{Transport: rt}
// tokenFn reads current token from cache/KMS; update cache on refresh
```
This way you don't recreate the TLS connection on refresh.
kevin: Also SDK-side: we should improve generator ergonomics. Two ideas: 1) document the RoundTripper approach in onboarding guide, 2) add a small helper on the Go SDK like StreamWithAuthRefresh that will detect transient connection resets during auth rotation and either retry transparently or return a typed ErrAuthRotated so callers can retry safely.
olivia: The current iterator returns: "rpc error: code = Canceled desc = stream terminated by peer" which looks like user cancel to many people. That confused our QA.
sam: Right — distinguishing user ctx cancel vs connection reset vs auth handshake abort would let apps handle it correctly. I propose adding typed errors ErrStreamConnReset and ErrStreamAuthRotate and emitting them when handshake or TCP-level reset is observed.
kevin: We'll need a small regression test against the runtime: simulate server side rejecting old token during mid-stream and ensure helper retries once. I'll add that to devex/ci.
devex-bot: created ticket DEVEX-843: update onboarding samples + sdk helper for auth-rotation handling (link) :spiral_notepad:
olivia: I'll open a docs PR showing both patterns: a) RoundTripper token provider, and b) explicit client recreate with clear retry loop and user-visible message. That should reduce confusion for newcomers.
kevin: Great. For the helper API sketch: StreamWithAuthRefresh(ctx, req, opts...) (returns iterator, cancelFn). Behavior: if transient auth-reset detected, either retry transparently once or surface ErrStreamAuthRotate depending on opts.RetryOnAuthRotate. Also add example using context.WithTimeout to avoid infinite retries.
sam: And add a short note in the generator README about "When to reuse transport vs recreate client" and a code snippet.
olivia: Thanks — I'll attach the repro logs in the ticket and link the PR. This should cut down on the onboarding support tickets. :+1:
